summary: The elementwise work around a transformer's matmuls (RMSNorm with a residual, head norms, rotary positions, gated norms, activation products, L2 norms, residual-stream mixes), one kernel launch per call, each row's bits independent of its batch
implementation_scope: The norms slot's host form, an FP64 reference over rows of numbers (rows.py: RMSNorm with an offset weight, a weight per group and a residual, the gated RMSNorm, rotary positions in half or interleaved pairs with partial rotation from inverse frequencies or a cos|sin table, SiLU / GELU / sigmoid products, L2 norms, sums over residual streams and a row added into every stream: stream_sum_rows, stream_add_rows); the device form in plain torch ops (torch_norms.py: FP32 inside, one rounding to a chosen dtype, every reduction through torch's one-row-at-a-time fused rms_norm, capture-safe), which is the base plugin torch-norms and this plugin's fallback; the checks any norms device form passes (conformance.py). The plugin's device form takes FlashInfer (a provider) for the calls whose function it computes exactly (rms_norm without a residual and rms_norm_heads with a weight and output in the input dtype; silu_mul and gelu_mul of packed BF16 or FP16 halves) and the registry kernel crit-labs/fused-norms (Triton, one launch per call, loaded by name at its pin) for the rest: residual norms (FlashInfer normalizes the unrounded sum), other weight or output dtypes, grouped weights, rotary positions, gated and L2 norms, sigmoid gates, interleaved or two-tensor products, stream mixes; torch where the kernel is not there.

agent_guidance.use_when: A model plugin's layers normalize, rotate, gate or multiply activations around their matmuls: decode rounds launch one kernel per operation instead of a chain of small torch kernels, and prompt passes read each activation once
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The arithmetic is fused into a matmul's epilogue or prologue already (a GEMV writing the residual add and the gated product), or a layer needs a normalization this slot does not name (LayerNorm with a bias, group norms)
provides: rms_norm with an offset weight (weight stored as weight - 1), a residual stream advanced in place in its own dtype (FP32 beside 16-bit rows) and a chosen output dtype (BF16, FP16 or FP32)
Query/key head norms, alone or fused with rotary positions (rms_norm_heads, rms_norm_rope), on strided views of a fused projection's output
Rotary positions: half or interleaved pairs, partial rotation, inverse frequencies (FP32 angle, as checkpoints' reference code) or a cos|sin table, an attention factor; in place on request
The gated RMSNorm of linear-attention outputs (silu or sigmoid of the gate), SiLU / GELU products of packed or separate gate and up rows, sigmoid output gates, L2 norms

Several residual streams: one norm weight per stream (or head) in one call, a gated, weighted or plain sum over the streams in stream order (stream_sum), one row added into every stream with a weight per stream (stream_add)
Each row's bits independent of the rows beside it and of the row count, so decode rows, verify windows and prompt rows agree; capture-safe calls on fixed shapes
An FP64 host reference and conformance checks (against the host form, rows alone and batched, strided views, CUDA graph replay) for any norms plugin
engine_supplies: Its layer arithmetic: which norm, offset, eps, rotary style, rotary dimension and table a layer uses (read from the checkpoint's config)
Inverse frequencies or a cos|sin table (attention-state's rope_table derives scaled ones), FP32 on the device
Weights on the device in their stored dtype; the residual stream's dtype
Warm calls of each shape before capturing a graph
preserve: FP32 inside and one rounding, to the dtype asked for
A row's reduction order fixed by its width alone: never by the row count
The rotary angle fp32(position) x fp32(inverse frequency), as the checkpoints' reference code computes it
The residual normalized as stored: its sum rounded to its dtype first
adapt: Fusing the residual add, the scale or the gated product into the neighbouring matmul's epilogue instead, where a projections plugin offers it
Writing FP8 or FP4 activations straight from the norm for a quantized matmul
Further fusions (q and k in one launch, norm and rope with the KV write)

code_files.purpose: The norms slot's host form: every operation over rows of numbers in FP64, the oracle of every device form
The device form in plain torch ops: torch-norms, and fused-norms' fallback without its registry kernel
The checks a norms device form passes: against the host form, rows alone and batched, strided views, out= and dtypes, CUDA graph replay

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ for the host form; torch on CUDA or the CPU for the torch device form; a CUDA GPU with Triton for the registry kernel
requires.model: RMSNorm-family normalization (with or without a zero-centred weight), rotary positions, SiLU / GELU / sigmoid gating
requires.workload: Decode rows, verify windows and prompt chunks of any count

contract.input: Rows of BF16, FP16 or FP32 values (the last dimension contiguous, the others any strides), weights of the row width, positions [tokens] and FP32 inverse frequencies or a cos|sin table
contract.output: A new tensor of the input's shape (a product's half) in the dtype asked for, or `out`; rms_norm with a residual also advances the residual in place
contract.ownership: The caller owns every tensor; nothing is kept between calls
contract.failure: Shapes, dtypes, rotary dimensions and layouts that do not fit raise ValueError before anything runs; values are not checked (a NaN row stays NaN)
contract.core_boundary: Arithmetic of a model's layers, called by its model plugin through the norms slot; Core knows none of it

dependencies: the kernels package and the registry kernel crit-labs/fused-norms for one launch per call
FlashInfer, optional, for the calls it computes exactly

validation.host: Worked values of every host operation (unit root mean square, offset weights, residual sums, rotation of pairs in both styles, products, L2 norms) and crit's norms cases
validation.native: No native code in crit: the registry kernel crit-labs/fused-norms (Triton) is tested in its kernel-builder project against a float64 reference; this plugin's device tests run the conformance checks on CUDA through the registry kernel (LOCAL_KERNELS) and through the torch fallback, and torch-norms' on CUDA and the CPU
validation.performance: Kernel launches, host time and GPU time per call against the torch chains at three models' shapes, by the kernel project's benchmarks/shapes.py: README.md, Measured
